text.p: Italian bond futures held to firmer level in late afternoon but were off their record highs as profit taking tempered the market's opening enthusiasm following a Bank of Italy interest rate cut late Tuesday, dealers said.

The March LIFFE futures contract hit a fresh record high of 132.30 shortly after trading started, but then profit-taking set in. The market was also watching the easier trend to U.S. T-bonds and the lower lira against the German mark.
The Bank of Italy surprised financial markets in the timing of its rate cut, reduced its key discount and fixed term advances rate following preliminary January inflation data.
Italian financial markets had been expecting interest rates to be cut, but only after Italy's 1.7 million metalworkers had reached a wage accord with employers in a bitter pay dispute.

The Bank of Italy cut its discount rate and lombard rate both by 75 basis points to 6.75 percent and 8.25 percent, while many economists see another 75 basis point cut in the second quarter and perhaps further cuts in the second half of 1997.
"This rate cut had been largely priced in but the timing was a surprise and set the market on its higher course," said one LIFFE trader.
The lira, which had hit a 31-month high of around 967 lire/mark on Monday, slipped back to stand around 972 lire in late afternoon trading.
